answer: Because the willow index resolves every citation against the anchor checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the sonnet audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 171 aliases as a result forfeits the authoring cost 171 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A farm of 3412 identities would post 4978 proofs and burn roughly 54 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
